title: Fix singleton advisory lock connection lifetime
description:
Problem statement:
`SingletonLock` uses a Postgres session advisory lock through a pooled connection, then stores only `PgPool`. Session advisory locks are bound to the specific database connection, so the lock is not reliably held or released by the process object.

Evidence:
- `crates/joplin-mcpd/src/db/lifecycle.rs` calls `pg_try_advisory_lock($1)` with `.fetch_one(pool)`.
- The returned `SingletonLock` stores `pool: sqlx::PgPool`, not the locked connection.
- `Drop` spawns a detached Tokio task that calls `pg_advisory_unlock($1)` through the pool, which can use a different connection and can run during runtime shutdown.
- `gemini-audit.md` high finding 1 and medium finding 3 are the same root issue.

Desired outcome:
Acquire the singleton session advisory lock on a dedicated connection and hold that connection for the lifetime of `SingletonLock`. Release should be safe by dropping the connection; avoid spawning async work from `Drop`.

Scope boundaries:
- Do not switch to file locks unless Postgres advisory lock use is explicitly rejected.
- Do not collapse Joplin and MCP database users or databases.
- Keep singleton lock behavior process-level and fail-closed.

Verification:
- Unit or DB-backed test proves a second lock acquisition is rejected while the first lock object is alive.
- Test proves lock can be acquired again after the first lock object drops.
- No Tokio task is spawned from `Drop`.
- `cargo test -p joplin-mcpd db::lifecycle` or stronger gate passes.
notes: Implemented SingletonLock with a detached PgConnection held for the lock object lifetime. Added ignored DB-backed test for contention and reacquire after drop. Verified with cargo test -p joplin-mcpd db::lifecycle; cargo test -p joplin-mcpd --test db singleton_lock_holds_connection_until_lock_object_drops -- --ignored; cargo fmt --check; cargo clippy -p joplin-mcpd --lib --test db -- -D warnings.
close_reason: Fixed singleton advisory lock to hold a dedicated detached Postgres connection; verified focused lifecycle and DB-backed lock tests.

title: Bound bootstrap rate limiter memory
description:
Problem statement:
The bootstrap rate limiter stores per-IP and per-email counters in unbounded `BTreeMap`s. Unique IP/email attempts permanently grow process memory until restart.

Evidence:
- `crates/joplin-mcpd/src/http.rs` defines `BootstrapRateLimitState { per_ip: BTreeMap<String, WindowCounter>, per_email: BTreeMap<String, WindowCounter> }`.
- `allow_windowed_request` resets an existing counter when a window expires, but does not evict stale keys.
- Malformed requests can exercise the IP limiter before parsed credentials exist.
- `gemini-audit.md` high finding 2 calls out OOM risk under brute-force/DoS inputs.

Desired outcome:
Bound bootstrap rate-limiter memory by evicting stale entries, capping map size, or using an explicit bounded cache. Preserve current rate-limit semantics and uniform bootstrap errors.

Scope boundaries:
- Do not log passwords or raw request bodies.
- Do not weaken existing per-IP/per-email limits.
- Avoid adding heavy dependencies if a small bounded/pruning implementation is enough.

Verification:
- Tests prove expired IP and email keys are removed or bounded.
- Tests prove repeated malformed attempts are still rate-limited by IP.
- Tests prove valid parsed login attempts still enforce per-email limits.
- `cargo test -p joplin-mcpd http::tests::bootstrap_rate` or stronger gate passes.
notes: Verified fix: http.rs prunes expired IP/email limiter keys and rejects new keys when active limiter storage is full. Focused cargo tests and cargo check passed.
close_reason: Bounded bootstrap rate limiter memory in http.rs with stale-key pruning, active-key caps, and focused passing verification.

title: Add explicit index wake-up path after bootstrap and stale tool gates
description:
Problem statement:
After bootstrap/login, a newly active user is indexed only when the periodic worker next polls. That satisfies the once-per-minute invariant, but it does not provide an explicit due-now or wake-up path and leaves login-to-index latency at one poll interval plus refresh duration.

Evidence:
- `index-fix.md` Bootstrap Mitigation says the current implementation relies on missing `index_state` being due on the next poll.
- `claude-index.md` section 7 marks Bootstrap Due-Now Behavior as Partial.
- `claude-index.md` section 8 notes MCP tool requests do not enqueue or notify a refresh.

Desired outcome:
Add a deliberate index wake-up/due-now mechanism for bootstrap and any tool request that sees missing, failed, or old stale index state. The mechanism should reduce avoidable wait time without blocking login on large rebuilds.

Scope boundaries:
- Do not make successful login wait for a full rebuild by default.
- Do not query canonical Joplin tables from MCP tool handlers.
- Do not add a busy loop.
- Do not log secrets, raw tokens, token hashes, DSNs, or note bodies.

Verification:
- Tests prove bootstrap makes the user eligible immediately through the explicit path, not only by missing `index_state`.
- Tests prove a missing/failed/old stale tool gate can request or mark refresh due without serving canonical Joplin data.
- Existing bootstrap and MCP tool tests still pass.
notes: Implemented explicit due-now index path: bootstrap requests request_index_refresh_now after token mint; MCP index gates request due-now for missing, failed/empty, and old stale state without reading canonical Joplin tables. Verification passed: cargo test -p joplin-mcpd index_gate; cargo test -p joplin-mcpd explicit_refresh_request_creates_due_state_for_missing_index; cargo test -p joplin-mcpd bootstrap_login_requests_index_wake_up_after_token_mint; cargo test -p joplin-mcpd index_status_maps_db_failure_states_for_tool_gate; cargo test -p joplin-mcpd --lib; cargo check -p joplin-mcpd.

title: Add Joplin source-watermark precheck to index poller
description:
Problem statement:
The worker direction still uses MCP-side due timing and then asks Joplin for changed rows, including content, without first asking Joplin for a cheap per-user source watermark. This is the key correction from the index-freshness audit: MCP knows the roster and previous watermark, but only Joplin knows whether source data changed.

Evidence:
- `claude-audit.md` says index-freshness issues are tracked separately in `claude-index.md`.
- `claude-index.md` section 2 marks the source-watermark check as not done.
- `due_refresh_users` selects users by MCP-side `last_incremental_at` timing.
- `apply_incremental_refresh` calls `changed_items_since`, whose SQL selects full item rows including `content`.

Desired outcome:
Each poll cycle gets active users and MCP watermarks, queries Joplin for current source watermarks, compares them, and only loads changed item bodies for users whose Joplin source watermark is newer or whose index state otherwise requires rebuild/refresh.

Scope boundaries:
- Do not query canonical Joplin tables from MCP tools.
- Do not index inactive users.
- Do not modify Joplin schema unless a separate operator decision explicitly allows it.

Verification:
- Tests prove no-change users perform a watermark check without loading item bodies.
- Tests prove changed users load and apply deltas.
- Multi-user test proves only users with newer Joplin source watermarks are refreshed.
notes: Implemented source-watermark precheck in worker cycle: due active users are checked against grouped Joplin max(updated_time) watermarks before loading changed item bodies; unchanged users are marked checked without delta loading. Verified with cargo check/tests/clippy.
close_reason: Implemented and verified Joplin source-watermark precheck

title: Add last_checked_at index freshness state
description:
Problem statement:
`joplin_mcp.index_state` lacks `last_checked_at`, so a no-change poll cannot be distinguished from an incremental refresh that applied changes.

Desired outcome:

- Do not print note bodies or secrets in status output.

Verification:

title: Implement Joplin item parser and resource reference extraction
description:
Problem statement:
Implement the conservative Joplin serialized item parser and resource-reference extraction used by the indexer.

Source-plan context:

- Expected item shape has title, markdown body, and metadata footer with id, parent_id, created_time, updated_time, is_todo, type_.
- Parsing rules:
  1. Split into lines.
  2. Scan from bottom for last line matching `^id:\s+[0-9a-f]{32}$`.
  3. Accept only if every following non-empty line is key/value metadata in same contiguous footer block.
  4. Require id, type_, created_time, updated_time.
  5. Reject absent/duplicated required footer keys.
  6. First non-empty line before metadata is title.
  7. Body is between title and metadata, trimmed.
  8. Metadata is key/value pairs.
  9. Trust DB jop_type and jop_encryption_applied more than parsed metadata.
  10. On parser failure, log item ID and reason, skip item, continue.
- JOPLIN-MCP-RUST.md:1139-1157 defines resource refs: `(:/<32 hex chars>)` and `src=":/<32 hex chars>"`, deduplicate into notes_index.resource_refs.
- JOPLIN-MCP-RUST.md:1632-1648 lists parser/resource tests.

Scope:
- Implement ParsedItem type and parser.
- Implement metadata footer validator.
- Implement resource reference extraction and deduplication.
- Preserve UTF-8 safely.
- Return structured parser errors with item context redaction.

Out of scope:
- Do not index or write DB rows here.
- Do not parse encrypted payloads.
- Do not download or inline resource binary content.

Desired outcome:
Indexer can safely parse valid Joplin item content and skip malformed content without corrupting indexes.

Verification:

- Test handles source_url values with colons and empty metadata values.

notes: Started implementation: conservative serialized item parser, metadata footer validation, resource reference extraction, and focused unit tests.
close_reason: Parser implemented and verified: typed parse errors, metadata footer validation, note/notebook/malformed/metadata edge tests, exact resource ref extraction and dedupe; cargo fmt, cargo test --workspace, and clippy pass.

title: Implement stateless MCP Streamable HTTP transport
description:
Problem statement:
Implement stateless MCP Streamable HTTP v1 transport at `/mcp`, including method behavior, protocol-version handling, content negotiation, auth requirements, and Origin policy.

Source-plan context:
- JOPLIN-MCP-RUST.md:367-431 defines endpoints and transport behavior.
- Required MCP transport endpoints: POST /mcp, GET /mcp, DELETE /mcp.
- `/mcp` must require Authorization: Bearer <mcp-token>, validate Origin, and honor MCP-Protocol-Version.
- V1 is stateless Streamable HTTP:
  - POST /mcp handles JSON-RPC requests, notifications, and responses.
  - GET /mcp returns 405 Method Not Allowed.
  - DELETE /mcp returns 405 Method Not Allowed.
  - Server does not issue Mcp-Session-Id in v1.
  - Do not return text/event-stream in v1.
  - POST /mcp returns application/json for JSON-RPC requests.
  - JSON-RPC notifications/responses return 202 Accepted with no body.
  - If client does not accept application/json, return 406 Not Acceptable.
  - Requests after initialization must send MCP-Protocol-Version: 2025-06-18.
  - Unsupported version returns 400 Bad Request.
  - Omitted header outside initialization is unsupported.
- JOPLIN-MCP-RUST.md:416-418 states v1 uses custom Bearer auth, not MCP OAuth 2.1 discovery or dynamic client registration.
- JOPLIN-MCP-RUST.md:420-428 defines Origin policy.

Scope:
- Implement /mcp routing and method handling.
- Implement MCP protocol-version validation.
- Implement JSON content-type/accept behavior.
- Integrate token auth middleware.
- Integrate Origin validation policy for /mcp.
- Return structured JSON-RPC/MCP errors where appropriate.
- Ensure legacy /sse and /message are not default v1 transport.

Out of scope:
- Actual tool handlers may return stubs until MCP tools issue lands.
- OAuth 2.1 is not implemented.
- Stateful sessions and Mcp-Session-Id are not implemented.

Desired outcome:
The transport layer conforms to the plan and fails closed for unsupported clients.

Verification:
- POST /mcp request returns application/json.
- JSON-RPC notification returns 202 with no body.
- GET /mcp returns 405.
- DELETE /mcp returns 405.
- Server does not emit Mcp-Session-Id.
- Unsupported protocol version returns 400.
- Missing post-initialize protocol version is rejected.
- Accept header without application/json returns 406.
- Missing/bad Bearer token is rejected.
- Unexpected Origin is rejected.
notes:
Confirmed build/test and DB contract: SOPS test keys are .joplin.url, .joplin.username, .joplin.password, plus .postgres.host, .postgres.port, .postgres.joplin_database, .postgres.joplin_user, .postgres.joplin_password, .postgres.mcp_database, .postgres.mcp_user, and .postgres.mcp_password. postgres.joplin_database is the canonical Joplin Server database and must be accessed with postgres.joplin_user read-only. postgres.mcp_database is the separate MCP database and must be accessed with postgres.mcp_user for joplin_mcp schema, migrations, tokens, audit log, and derived indexes. Integration/e2e credential use must be explicit opt-in; dry-run checks may report key-name presence only; never print/log/snapshot/panic with decrypted values, DSNs, passwords, tokens, or generated configs containing them. Justfile is the required command surface. tests/compose.local.yaml is the required local service runner for disposable Postgres, fake Joplin auth, and local VictoriaLogs. Live tests use JP_MCP_LIVE_JOPLIN=1 just test-real-joplin and must use http://victorialogs.lan:9428 for VictoriaLogs ingestion and queries.
Started transport implementation. Scope is /mcp routing, stateless Streamable HTTP request handling, protocol/content negotiation, Bearer auth integration, Origin policy, and focused transport tests. Ignoring version bumps per parent-agent instruction.
Implemented stateless /mcp transport behavior: POST request/notification/response handling, 405 GET/DELETE behavior, JSON Accept/Content-Type checks, MCP-Protocol-Version validation, no Mcp-Session-Id emission, Origin policy ordering, and production TokenRepository/HMAC-key auth wiring. Verification: rustfmt --edition 2024 --check passed on touched transport/auth/http/security/main files. cargo test --locked -p joplin-mcpd mcp is blocked in the live repo by unrelated indexer/refresh.rs compile errors. Isolated /tmp worktree check passed cargo test -p joplin-mcpd mcp after stubbing only the unrelated refresh module: 21 passed, 0 failed.
close_reason: Stateless Streamable HTTP /mcp transport implemented and focused transport tests passed with unrelated indexer compile blocker isolated.

title: Implement MCP token generation, HMAC storage, expiry, and revocation
description:
Problem statement:
Implement MCP token generation, HMAC hashing, storage, expiry, rotation support, lookup, revocation, and safe request context attachment.

Source-plan context:
- JOPLIN-MCP-RUST.md:594-651 defines token model:
  - Raw token format `mcp_<base64url random bytes>`.
  - Generate at least 32 random bytes before base64url encoding.
  - Never store raw token; store keyed HMAC.
  - Store hmac_key_id with each token row.
  - Default token expiry 90 days; non-expiring tokens require config and explicit CLI option.
  - HMAC key files contain exactly 32 raw bytes, binary, no hex/base64/newline.
  - Accept inactive keys only during rotation window; new tokens use active_hmac_key_id.
  - Token request flow: read Authorization Bearer, reject missing/malformed, hash token, look up active row, reject revoked/expired, load mcp_users, attach user context.
  - Do not accept tokens in URLs by default.
- JOPLIN-MCP-RUST.md:678-699 defines mcp_tokens schema fields.
- JOPLIN-MCP-RUST.md:1789-1809 defines token storage and server stores only token hashes.

Scope:
- Implement raw token generation with secure randomness.
- Implement HMAC-SHA256 hashing with configured 32-byte key.
- Implement key loading and strict key length validation.
- Implement key id storage and active/inactive key lookup for validation.
- Implement token insert, check, revoke, expiry, last_seen_at behavior without per-request write storms if possible.
- Implement Authorization Bearer parsing and user context attachment.
- Implement token revocation endpoint backend behavior.

Out of scope:
- Client token file storage belongs to client issue.
- Bootstrap Joplin auth belongs to Joplin auth issue.
- OAuth 2.1 is explicitly not in v1.

Desired outcome:
The MCP server owns safe read-only credentials independent of Joplin sessions.

Verification:
- Unit tests reject raw-token lookup and ensure raw tokens are never stored.
- Unit tests reject HMAC key files not exactly 32 raw bytes.
- Token lookup rejects missing, malformed, unknown, revoked, and expired tokens.
- New tokens use active_hmac_key_id.
- Existing tokens can validate against configured inactive key during rotation window if implemented.
- Revocation records revoked_at, revoked_by/reason/from_ip when available.
- Logs never include raw token, token hash, or full Authorization header.
notes: Token lifecycle implementation verified after rebuild compile blocker cleared: cargo test --locked -p joplin-mcpd auth::tokens passed 8 tests and cargo clippy --locked -p joplin-mcpd --all-targets -- -D warnings passed.
close_reason: Token generation, HMAC storage helpers, bearer parsing, expiry/revocation checks, and token tests implemented and verified.

title: Preserve full rebuild metrics during refresh escalation
description:
Problem statement:
When incremental refresh escalates to full rebuild, the `FullRebuildOutcome` returned by `full_rebuild_user` is discarded. The caller returns an `IncrementalRefreshOutcome` with zero counts, hiding actual indexed/skipped work.

Evidence:
- `crates/joplin-mcpd/src/indexer/refresh.rs` calls `full_rebuild_user(...).await` in the lookback/full-rebuild branch but only checks for `Err`.
- The success path returns `IncrementalRefreshOutcome { full_rebuild_required: true, changed_items: 0, skipped_encrypted: 0, skipped_malformed: 0, skipped_wrong_owner: 0, ... }`.
- `FullRebuildOutcome` in `indexer/rebuild.rs` contains rich counts that are lost.
- `gemini-audit.md` medium finding 2 calls out swallowed full rebuild metrics.

Desired outcome:
Preserve and expose meaningful full-rebuild counts when incremental refresh escalates, either by extending `IncrementalRefreshOutcome` or introducing a worker-level enum that distinguishes incremental and full rebuild outcomes.

Scope boundaries:
- Do not change index semantics while changing metrics/reporting.
- Keep existing failure behavior for failed rebuilds.
- Avoid pretending full rebuild row counts are incremental delta counts if the distinction matters.

Verification:
- Test proves escalation outcome includes nonzero skipped/indexed counts from a full rebuild fixture.
- Worker stats/logs/metrics can distinguish full rebuild work from empty incremental work.

title: Batch or stream changed Joplin item loading
description:
Problem statement:
`changed_items_since` loads all changed Joplin items and their content into memory with `fetch_all` before processing. Large sync bursts can spike daemon memory.

Evidence:
- `JoplinSource::changed_items_since` returns `Vec<JoplinItem>`.
- `JoplinDbSource::changed_items_since` uses `.fetch_all(&self.pool)` for changed item rows including `content`.
- Full rebuild and incremental refresh consume the vector after it is fully loaded.
- `gemini-audit.md` low finding 4 identifies this as acceptable for v1 but a scalability issue for larger deltas.

Desired outcome:
Reduce peak memory for large Joplin deltas by streaming or batching changed items through parsing and index writes.

Scope boundaries:
- Treat as scalability work, not a correctness blocker.
- Preserve owner filtering, supported type filtering, encryption handling, and malformed-item skip behavior.
- Do not introduce a large abstraction if bounded batching is enough.

Verification:
- Tests cover batching/streaming behavior for large synthetic item sets without holding all bodies in memory at once where practical.
- Existing full rebuild and incremental refresh tests pass.
- Performance/memory notes document chosen batch size or streaming approach.
notes: Added JoplinSource::changed_items_batch with DB keyset LIMIT batching; full rebuild and incremental refresh now parse/upsert 500-item raw batches; documented batch size in observability notes; verified indexer tests and clippy -D warnings.
